I survived a headon collision with a Bus and live to tell my tale AMA
I was on foot. Heading to my grandmothers from school.

Multiple skull fractures including an eye socket. Swelling of the brain due to blunt trauma. Non Weight Bearing Pelvic Fractures. Broken Femur to the right leg. Ligament damage to the left knee. Some serious scrapes all across my right leg, lower arms and the back of my hands. The busses metal front bumper got a decent dent, the window was cracked. My laptop was in its case and had a convenient habit of shifting to my front. I think thats the reason for the pelvic fractures and possibly why I'm still living since it took the brunt of the hit.

Wow...

When did this happen? Are you still recovering?

Early 2013

There was head trauma and I had a seizure once or twice. they took a few scans of my head and discovered some scarring in the frontal lobe (I think its that part). Apparently it wont be clear how bad the damage is until my body stops developing mid 20's. But physically I am fine and I am perfectly capable of intelligent and coherent thought. Due to the ligament damage however I can't just go and play soccer or rugby. Martial arts would put a fair bit of stress on it too. And with any leg exercises I need to be careful, take it easy, and gradually build up knee strength to support the ligaments.

I also put less weight on the importance of sanity these days and I have more trouble gathering the motivation to do anything. Thats basically the only apparent long term effect that's emerged so far. I do however worry I'm developing arthritis early on. Sometimes my legs like to ache around the knee areas and at the part of my leg where it broke and a metal rod now lies inside it. Oddly enough a new bone/sort of formed in my pelvis

I may need you to define what you mean by Entourage. But as for feeling different, any experience like that will change you. It's actually surprising the clarity of thought you have when you fully wake up from something like that. Even with all the stress and confusion of wondering how the fuck you got from walking home from high school to the major trauma ward of a hospital 2 hours drive away. It was probably the first time I truly saw the world we've built for what it is. I remember using humor to hide how fucking terrified and alone I felt. Even with my mother there every day. But in all honesty I've never looked at the world the same again.
